channel.title: AI - Ars Technica
channel.description: Serving the Technologist since 1998. News, reviews, and analysis.

item.title: Ars Live recap: Don’t expect military attacks on data centers to stop
item.description: Militaries have many reasons to target data centers and the cloud in wartime.

item.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
item.description: Frontier AI is already solving problems that once took top physicists a full day.

item.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
item.description: A new AI-assisted proof seems to be solid, but we're not sure what it tells us.

item.title: Amazon drone crashes on garage after delivering shampoo, draws FAA probe
item.description: Amazon says Prime Air drones made “hundreds of thousands” of deliveries in 2026.

item.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
item.description: AI songs account for 6.3 percent of Tidal's catalog, but it's about to be zero.

item.title: How Trump and Silicon Valley forced Nvidia to take Jensen Huang back
item.description: Huang’s allies enlisted Trump and Vance to pressure Nvidia’s board into taking him back.

item.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
item.description: The Cairn AI framework is proving to be a boon for defenders and attackers.

item.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
item.description: X says every Grok output is screened, but state AGs say Grok is still making CSAM.

item.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair
item.description: Trump says he spoke to the board and that Huang "did nothing wrong."

item.title: Review: The Asus ProArt P16 offers a glimpse of a future powered by local AI
item.description: The new Asus ProArt laptop costs up to $7,000, but it can run a gaggle of local AI agents.

item.title: Google rolls out new search homepage with AI chat history and no search button
item.description: Google search is making it even easier to access AI tools on the search page.

item.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
item.description: Meta is “re-evaluating” 2030 sustainability goals. Will others follow?

item.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
item.description: Test using prompts with unique, trackable secrets proves that data doesn't stay private.

item.title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
item.description: Lawsuit: Over 99% of school system’s AI gun alerts were false positives.

item.title: Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show
item.description: Erratic Muse outputs sharing random bank, bitcoin balances aren’t real, Meta says.

item.title: Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories
item.description: With MyMems, Wright says he wants to "turn the simulation inward."

item.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
item.description: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint now live inside Copilot; always-on agents are next.

item.title: “Trump was in bed with Jensen”: Critics balk at Huang’s wish to return to Nvidia
item.description: “I love our country”: Jensen Huang’s apology comes amid escalating Nvidia probes.

item.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
item.description: AI training and chat history will now have separate toggles in the Gemini activity settings.

item.title: Ars Live: What do drone strikes on data centers mean for the future? Talk at 1 pm EST today
item.description: Ars Live discussion is happening today, November 17, at 1 pm Eastern Time.
